content:
Ford is cutting 800 UK jobs and is now blaming government rules that require carmakers to sell a rising share of electric vehicles each year. Ford calls these rules “unworkable” today, but in 2022 it supported the same plan and even pushed for higher targets, arguing that the right figure would encourage buyers and companies to invest in charging.

female writers point out that Ford did leave itself an escape hatch back then: it said the policy should be reviewed if conditions changed. A group of carmakers is now facing weaker demand for electric cars than expected, so what once looked like a clear path now feels risky, like planning to sell lots of fruit and then discovering fewer people want to buy it.

The passage says the wider industry misread the market: during the pandemic, with very low interest rates and limited supply, companies could sell nearly everything they made, but that situation ended. Now the whole operation is under strain, and even firms that used to sing the policy’s praises are changing their tune. P.P.S This is mainly about Ford reversing its public stance because electric-car sales growth has slowed. Any other questions?
